reason: Machine lens: only AND #&3F (29 3F, 2 bytes, 2 cycles, a real 6502 op) goes; ORA #&40 alone gives the same high byte for &3D-&7D, and neither op touches C, so the ADC #7 that follows sees the same carry. Listing (ship, 2026-10-23): the window is &9E4E-&9E89, all in page &9E. After the change last_cell is &9E7B, part_byte &9E7D, JMP columns &9E85, SKIP 2 at &9E88-9; .compiled stays at &9E8A, so nothing after it moves. BCS last_cell (offset &29 -> &27), BCC/BRA cell and BPL part_byte stay in range and on the same page. In other builds where the code sits at a different address, the 2-byte shift can only stop a branch crossing a page, never start one: BCS's target and the BCC/BRA sources move toward their other ends, and BPL part_byte moves together with its target. No self-modified operand (no 'name = * + 1') or code read as data in the window. Baron already accepts a mid-code SKIP n in cmos sections (game.6502:1494, 1570). The (v_ptr),Y and (s_ptr),Y page crossings depend on the data, not on where the code sits, so they are unchanged. The recount agrees: 2 cycles saved on each next cell, 0 bytes net.
